samples.summary: `isDeferred` misses the non-gating findings of an ADVISORY lens, a population the panel already supports out of diff
samples.evidence: `isDeferred` treats a finding as deferred only when `normalizeSeverity` is non-blocking, or when `lane === "backlog"`. But a lens whose manifest entry says `gating` is anything other than `"blocking"` never gates at all: `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:957` computes `const blocking = String(lens.gating ?? 'blocking') === 'blocking'` and only pushes blocking lenses into `required` (line 963-964), and `scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:3161` passes `advisory: !blocking` into `writeVerdict`, whose check always reports success. Such a lens's critical/major findings are written into `verdict.json` with `lane: "blocking"` (review-panel.mjs:3006 `gatingFindings(merged)` / annotateFindings), so they are findings "the gate did not act on" that this channel silently omits — the exact population it exists to record. Latent today because all six entries in scripts/agent/lenses/lenses.json carry `"gating": "blocking"`; it becomes wrong the first time an advisory lens is added, and nothing in deferred-findings.test.mjs covers a lens-level gating flag. The fix belongs on the new code: `collectDeferred`/`readLensFindings` would need the manifest's `gating` (which it already reads) to be carried into the deferred predicate.
searchedFor: read scripts/agent/deferred-findings.test.mjs for any advisory-lens case

samples.summary: The new advisory check run lands in loop-status's non-lens "checks" bucket, so the dashboard's CI cell can read ✅ from it alone
samples.evidence: `buildRounds` splits a commit's check runs into lens runs (manifest names) and `const others = runs.filter((r) => !names.has(r.name));` (scripts/agent/loop-status.mjs:207), then renders the round's CI cell from `others`: no RED_CONCLUSIONS and all completed → `checks = "success"` (lines 209-213). `agent-deferred-findings` is created by the github-actions app, `status: 'completed'`, `conclusion: 'neutral'`, so it passes the app filter at line 192 and is counted as a non-lens CI check. Consequence: a round whose commit carries no other non-lens checks now renders ✅ (previously `none`/`—`) purely because of an advisory record that says nothing about CI. It cannot flip a failure to success, and it cannot mint a phantom round (line 194 still requires a lens run), so impact is confined to a misleading cell — but the pair `agent-deferred-findings`/`others` was not considered by the change, and the same bucket is reused by panel-round-comment.mjs:212 via `roundNumberFor`.

samples.summary: Two gates read a commit's check runs UNPAGINATED (`?per_page=100`); this adds one more run per round to that first-page window
samples.evidence: `mark-ready.mjs:151` fetches `repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/${sha}/check-runs?per_page=100` with no `--paginate` and then decides promotion from `allRequiredPassed(data.check_runs ?? [], REQUIRED_CHECKS)` (line 155); `set-state.mjs:232` does the same and derives `lensBlocked` from the first page only (line 233-235). Every panel round now creates a 7th check run on the head sha instead of 6, and re-runs of CI/panel on the SAME sha accumulate check runs, so this change moves both consumers one step closer to a first-page overflow in which a required `agent-review-<lens>` run is not in the response and the gate reads it as not passed (fail-closed for promotion, but `lensBlocked` would read false). I could not establish that any real commit approaches 100 check runs — ci.yml has ~6 jobs plus small matrices — so this is a suspicion about an aggravated latent limit, not a demonstrated break. Confirming it needs a count of check runs on a heavily re-run agent PR head.
